title: Tangerine: a new family of Starships from lichen-forming fungi
authors: Tagirdzhanova G; Brown NE; Bucknell AH; Cameron ES; Cameron ES; Finn RD; Blaxter M; McDonald MC; Gluck-Thaler E; Talbot NJ
one_liner_zh: 该文研究地衣真菌中的转座元件Starships及其基因组进化，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Lichens are symbiotic associations between filamentous fungi and photosynthetic micro-organisms, such as green algae and/or cyanobacteria, that result in a single anatomically-complex structure that can thrive in environments inhospitable to most organisms, including arctic tundra, high mountains, and deserts. Recent evidence suggests that lichens may be even more complex than previously appreciated, containing multiple microbial constituents, but how genomes of the principal fungal symbiont (which provides the majority of biomass in lichen tissue) have been shaped during evolution is largely unexplored. Recently, giant transposable elements called Starships have been found in many genomes of filamentous fungi, but to which extent they occur in lichen-forming fungi is not known. In this report, we describe a Starship element from the lichen fungus Xanthoria parietina . This element, named Tangerine , contains several genes that have signatures of horizontal gene transfer from non-lichen-forming fungi, most likely from black yeasts of the Chaetothyriales, that are often lichen-associated. Repetitive sequences carried by Tangerine , and found in other sites in Xanthoria genomes, are affected by repeat-induced point mutation (RIP), a mechanism of genome defense against transposable elements, consistent with fungal sexual reproduction which always precedes new lichen formation by Xanthoria . Tangerine ’s “captain” belongs to a newly defined family of tyrosine recombinases specific to lichen-forming Lecanoromycetes. Several other captain clades have signatures of horizontal gene transfer between distantly related lichen-forming fungi and non-mycobiont lichen-associated fungi. We speculate that Starships may play a significant, yet hitherto unrecognized role, in lichen genome evolution and provide a roadmap for further investigation.
abstract_zh: 地衣是丝状真菌与光合微生物（如绿藻和/或蓝细菌）之间的共生联合，形成单一解剖学上复杂的结构，能在大多数生物无法生存的环境中繁茂生长，包括北极冻原、高山和沙漠。近期证据表明，地衣可能比先前认知的更为复杂，包含多种微生物组分，但主要真菌共生体（其提供地衣组织中大部分生物量）的基因组在进化过程中如何被塑造，在很大程度上尚未被探索。最近，在多种丝状真菌基因组中发现了名为Starships的巨型转座元件，但它们在地衣形成真菌中的分布程度尚不清楚。在本报告中，我们描述了一个来自地衣真菌Xanthoria parietina的Starship元件。该元件名为Tangerine，包含多个具有水平基因转移特征的基因，这些基因源自非地衣形成真菌，最可能来自常与地衣相关的Chaetothyriales目黑色酵母。Tangerine携带的重复序列，以及在Xanthoria基因组其他位点发现的重复序列，受到重复诱导点突变（repeat-induced point mutation, RIP）的影响，这是一种针对转座元件的基因组防御机制，与真菌有性生殖一致，而Xanthoria新地衣形成前总是发生有性生殖。Tangerine的“captain”属于一个新定义的酪氨酸重组酶家族，该家族特异于地衣形成型Lecanoromycetes。其他几个captain分支具有水平基因转移的特征，涉及远缘相关的地衣形成真菌和非地衣共生体的地衣相关真菌。我们推测，Starships可能在地衣基因组进化中扮演重要但迄今未被认识的角色，并为进一步研究提供了路线图。
